sanskrit: endro bāhubhyām abharac cikitvān apo devīr varuṇāya prajānan | tam ādityā abhy aṣiñcanta sarve rājānam ugraṃ bṛhate raṇāya tā na āpo rājasūyā avantu ||
english: Indra, knowing, carried the divine waters with both arms for Varuṇa; all the Ādityas consecrated him, that fierce king, for the great battle. May those waters, the rājasūya waters, be favorable to us.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇā iti catasraḥ ||
english: [The four verses beginning with] 'Of golden hue' — [rubric indicating four verses of the Golden-Hued Waters hymn to be recited here].

sanskrit: apo devīr madhumatīr agṛhṇata- -ūrjasvatī rājasūyā mayobhuvaḥ | yābhir mitrāvaruṇāv abhyasiñcan tāḥ (…) ||
english: The divine waters, honey-sweet, yielding strength, the rājasūya waters that bring well-being — those with which Mitra and Varuṇa were consecrated — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: varuṇena preṣitā yanti śubhrā utsaṃ devīr dadhate yā hiraṇyayam | yā brahmaṇā punate saṃvidānās tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those bright ones, sent forth by Varuṇa, move onward — divine waters that bear the golden spring; those that purify in concert with the sacred utterance — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: apaḥ samudrād divam ud vahanti divas pṛthivīm abhi yāḥ sṛjanti | yābhir īśānā marutaś caranti tāḥ (…) ||
english: The waters that carry from the ocean up to heaven, and from heaven release themselves upon the earth; those with which the sovereign Maruts roam — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: yā amṛtaṃ bibhrati yā madhu priyaṃ yā agṛbhṇan ṛṣayo devasakhye | yābhir indram aty anayann arātīs tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those that bear immortality, that carry sweet honey, those that the seers seized in the companionship of the gods; those by which Indra was led beyond his foes — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: yā jīvadhanyā dhanam utpṛṇanti devāyate dāśuṣe martyāya | yāsāṃ payo akṣitam akṣitānāṃ tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those that fill wealth to the brim for the mortal who is devout and generous, who desires the gods; whose milk is inexhaustible among inexhaustible things — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: hiraṇyaupaśā dhvajanīḥ punānā yāḥ samudram abhyarcanti dhenavaḥ | yāḥ parjanyo vahaty antarikṣe tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those that have golden ornaments, that bear banners, purifying themselves — the milk-cows that flow toward the ocean; those that Parjanya carries in the atmosphere — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: rathantare bṛhati gīyamāne kṣatraṃ jinvanti pra tiranty āyuḥ | yābhis trayān vājino vājayanti tāḥ (…) ||
english: When the Rathantara and the Bṛhat sāmans are sung, they invigorate lordly power and extend life; those by which the swift steeds are made to course in the three contests — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: yābhiḥ saha vṛtrahā somam indro vasor īśāno apibat sutasya | yāḥ sapta ṛṣayaḥ kavayaḥ punanti tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those in whose company Indra the Vṛtra-slayer, lord of riches, drank the pressed Soma; those that the seven seers, the inspired poets, purify — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: sapta ṛṣayo bharatam abhy aṣiñcann āsmin rāṣṭram adadhur dakṣiṇāvat | prajāyai manum asumavanta devās tāḥ (…) ||
english: The seven seers consecrated Bharata; they established the realm in him, rich in sacrificial fees; the gods endowed Manu with vital breath for his offspring — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: yābhir yajñaṃ prāñcam ukṣayanti dhīrā yābhiḥ somaṃ madhupṛcaṃ punanti | yābhir idaṃ jīvati viśvam ejat tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those with which the wise ones sprinkle the eastward-facing sacrifice; those with which they purify the honey-mixed Soma; those by which all this stirring universe lives — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: yāsāṃ stokā madhumayā babhūvur ghṛtaṃ saṃjñānaṃ madhu pinvate yāḥ | yāḥ soma āpaḥ praṇayanti brahmaṇā tāḥ (…) ||
english: Those whose drops have become full of honey; those that swell with ghee-rich agreement and with sweetness; those waters that Soma leads forth by the sacred word — [may those waters be favorable to us].

sanskrit: yāsāṃ pador ājyaṃ vājinaṃ tu somasya prasavam anu yāḥ pavante | antarvatīs taruṇavatsā ghṛtācīs tā na āpo rājasūyā avantu ||
english: Those at whose feet the strength-giving ghee flows; those that purify themselves in the wake of Soma's outpouring; pregnant ones, with young calves, rich in ghee — may those waters, the rājasūya waters, be favorable to us.

sanskrit: ajījananta matayaḥ svarvida ā brahmaṇā sūktadheyāny aguḥ | asūṣuta rājasūyāḥ payāṃsi prāsāvīd devaḥ savitā bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: Inspired thoughts were born; those that know the way to heaven came forward through the sacred word to the places of the well-spoken hymns. The rājasūya waters gave forth their streams of milk; the god Savitṛ impelled all the worlds.

sanskrit: somo rājā bhavo rājā paśupatiḥ paśūnāṃ varuṇo dhṛtavrataḥ | ye rājasūye asūyanta devās te te kṣatraṃ dadhatv āyur ojaḥ ||
english: Soma the king, Bhava the king, Paśupati lord of beasts, Varuṇa the steadfast in vow — those gods who were present at the rājasūya, let them bestow upon you sovereign power, long life, and might.

sanskrit: āsthād ud asthād ajaniṣṭa vipro mṛdho vy āsthad aśasīta bāhū | āre avādhiṣṭa nirṛtiṃ parācaiḥ samapṛkta raśmibhiḥ sūryaś ca ||
english: He stood up, he rose, the inspired sage was born; he stepped over his foes, he wielded his arms in battle; he thrust Nirṛti far away toward the distant quarters; and with the sun he mingled, with its rays.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ tvāvarohantaṃ divataḥ pṛthivīm iva | apaśyam asyantaṃ rudraṃ nīlagrīvaṃ śikhaṇḍinam ||
english: I beheld you descending, as if from heaven to earth; I beheld Rudra, the blue-throated, the crest-bearing, as he cast his shaft.

sanskrit: diva ugro 'vārukṣat praty aṣṭhād bhūmyām adhi | janāsaḥ paśyatemaṃ nīlagrīvaṃ vilohitam ||
english: The dreadful one climbed down from heaven and stood established upon the earth. O people, behold this one — the blue-throated, the deeply crimson.

sanskrit: eṣa aity avīrahā rudro jalāṣabheṣajī | vi te kṣepam anīnaśad vātīkāro vy etu te ||
english: This Rudra, the healer with cooling medicines, the destroyer of no man's hero, comes hither. He has made your trembling to vanish utterly; may your feverish agitation depart.

sanskrit: namas te bhava bhāmāya namas te bhava manyave | namas te astu bāhūbhyām uto ta iṣave namaḥ ||
english: Homage to you, O Bhava, in your brilliance; homage to you, O Bhava, in your wrath. Homage to you be unto both your arms, and homage also to your arrow.

sanskrit: yām iṣaṃ giriśanta haste bibharṣy astave | śivāṃ giriśa tāṃ kṛṇu mā hiṃsīḥ puruṣān mama ||
english: That arrow which you hold in your hand to shoot, O lord of the mountain — make it auspicious, O Giriśa; do not harm my people.

sanskrit: śivena vacasā tvā giriśācchā vadāmasi | yathā naḥ sarvam ij jagad ayakṣmaṃ sumano asat ||
english: With auspicious speech we address you, O Giriśa; so that for us all this world may be free of consumption and of glad spirit.

sanskrit: yā ta iṣuḥ śivatamā śivaṃ babhūva te dhanuḥ | śivā śaravyā yā tava tayā no mṛḍa jīvase ||
english: Your arrow that is most auspicious, your bow that has become auspicious, your quiver that is auspicious — with that grant us ease, that we may live.

sanskrit: yā te rudra śivā tanūr aghorāpāpakāśinī | tayā nas tanvā śantamayā giriśantābhi cākaśa ||
english: That form of yours, O Rudra, which is auspicious, which is not terrible, which does not reveal evil — with that most tranquil body, O Giriśa, shine upon us.

sanskrit: asau yas tāmro aruṇa uta babhrur vilohitaḥ | ye ceme abhito rudrā dikṣu śritāḥ sahasraśo 'vaiṣāṃ heḍa īmahe ||
english: That one yonder who is copper-red, tawny, and deeply crimson — and these Rudras here on all sides, stationed in the directions by thousands — from their wrath we seek protection.

sanskrit: adṛśaṃ tvāvarohantaṃ nīlagrīvaṃ vilohitam | uta tvā gopā adṛśann uta tvodāhāryaḥ | uto tvā viśvā bhūtāni tasmai dṛṣṭāya te namaḥ ||
english: I beheld you descending, the blue-throated, the deeply crimson; the herdsmen too beheld you, and so did the women fetching water; all beings too beheld you — homage to you, to you thus seen.
